name: Hanging leg raise
pattern: Hanging from a bar (or supported in a captain's chair), the knees or straight legs lift and the pelvis curls up toward the ribs.
setup: Hang from a bar with straight arms, hands shoulder width, or rest your forearms in a captain's chair.
Pull your shoulders slightly down so you don't hang loose.

steps.text: Raise your knees (or straight legs) to hip height.
Keep going: tilt your pelvis up so your knees rise toward your chest.
Lower under control until your legs hang straight, without swinging.

cues.cue: Curl the pelvis up, don't just lift the legs.
cues.why: Hanging knee-ups were among the top exercises for rectus abdominis and internal oblique activity, but only when the pelvis curls.

cues.cue: No swing: pause at the bottom.
cues.why: Momentum takes over the lift and reduces abdominal work.
An active hang steadies the trunk; the lats work hard in this lift.

cues.cue: Bend the knees to make it easier, straighten to make it harder.
cues.why: Straight legs make a longer lever and a harder exercise.

breathing: Breathe out as you lift, in as you lower.

tempo.note: Lift in 1 second, lower in 2, pause before the next rep.

mistakes.name: Swinging
mistakes.looks: The body rocks back and forth and the legs fly up.
mistakes.fix: Pause dead still at the bottom of each rep.
mistakes.why: Momentum, not the abs, lifts the legs.

mistakes.name: Legs stop at hip height
mistakes.looks: Thighs reach level but the pelvis never tilts up.
mistakes.fix: Keep lifting: knees toward the chest.
mistakes.why: Without the pelvic curl it is mostly a hip flexor lift.

mistakes.name: Shoulders shrug to the ears
mistakes.looks: The head sinks between the arms.
mistakes.fix: Pull the shoulders down before you lift.
mistakes.why: A passive hang strains the shoulder and lets the trunk wobble.

safety: Shoulder pain: use a captain's chair or ab straps instead of a hang.
Low back pain: start with bent knees and stop at hip height.

variants.change: Straight legs: harder; toes-to-bar brings the feet up to the hands.
Forearms on pads: no grip demand, less shoulder load.
Knees lift to one side or circle: more oblique work.
Load at the feet makes the lever heavier.

subtypes.name: Toes to bar
subtypes.change: Legs keep rising until the feet (or knees) touch the bar; the trunk leans back.

subtypes.name: Captain's chair
subtypes.change: Back against the pad, forearms on the arm rests; same leg path.

motion.basis: Default is the bent-knee hanging raise. All angles estimated from the technique; activation ranking from escamilla2006 and mcgill2015.

sources.cite: Escamilla RF et al. Electromyographic analysis of traditional and nontraditional abdominal exercises: implications for rehabilitation and training. Phys Ther. 2006;86(5):656-671.

McGill S, Andersen J, Cannon J. Muscle activity and spine load during anterior chain whole body linkage exercises: the body saw, hanging leg raise and walkout from a push-up. J Sports Sci. 2015;33(4):419-426.
Andersson EA, Nilsson J, Ma Z, Thorstensson A. Abdominal and hip flexor muscle activation during various training exercises. Eur J Appl Physiol Occup Physiol. 1997;75(2):115-123.

Juker D, McGill S, Kropf P, Steffen T. Quantitative intramuscular myoelectric activity of lumbar portions of psoas and the abdominal wall during a wide variety of tasks. Med Sci Sports Exerc. 1998;30(2):301-310.
